title: Simulations of the Evolving Ozone Layer: Implications for the Early Earth, Exoplanets, and the Search For Life
venue: Submitted to R. Soc. Open Sci. · arXiv:2610.18864
tldr: Four widely used 1D atmosphere codes and a 3D climate model are run on the same oxygen-poor Earths. The 1D codes predict more ozone than the 3D model, increasingly so as oxygen drops, which changes predicted surface UV damage by up to ~8× and the ozone features in exoplanet spectra.

question.short: Do 1D and 3D models agree on how thick the ozone layer was when Earth had less oxygen?
question.detail: Ozone shields life from UV, and its history is usually computed with fast 1D photochemical models. The authors test how far four open-source 1D codes disagree with a 3D chemistry-climate model (WACCM6) across 0.1–150% of today's O₂, why, and what that does to habitability and exoplanet predictions.

answer.short: No. They agree at today's O₂, but at ≤10% O₂ the 1D codes predict thicker ozone than WACCM6, and the gap grows as O₂ falls.
answer.detail: There is no single cause: O₂ photolysis, chemical networks and rates, water vapour, and 3D transport all contribute. The gap propagates to up to ~8× differences in surface DNA damage and to visibly different O₃ features in exoplanet spectra.

why_important.headline: 1D models underpin habitability claims
why_important.detail: Early-Earth UV environments and exoplanet biosignature predictions mostly come from 1D photochemical codes.

why_important.headline: Ozone shaped life on the surface
why_important.detail: The ozone layer controls how much damaging UV reaches the surface, so its thickness through Earth's history matters for evolution.

why_important.headline: Few 1D–3D comparisons exist
why_important.detail: Only a handful of studies compared 1D models with 3D models, and no single model includes every relevant process.

why_important.headline: Billion-dollar telescopes will look for ozone
why_important.detail: HWO (~$11B) and LIFE (~$1B) plan to search for O₃ as a sign of life, so model disagreements matter for interpretation.

background.headline: Oxygen rose in steps
background.detail: O₂ rose at the Great Oxidation Event (~2.4 Ga), sat around 0.1–10% of today's level through much of the Proterozoic, then rose again to 10–150% in the Phanerozoic.

background.headline: How ozone is made and destroyed
background.detail: UV splits O₂ into O atoms, which combine with O₂ to make O₃ (Chapman mechanism). Catalytic cycles of HOₓ and NOₓ radicals destroy it.

background.headline: Schumann–Runge bands are hard to model
background.detail: O₂ absorption at 175–205 nm is strongly temperature dependent. Only the Kasting model has the newer correlated-k treatment.

background.headline: WACCM6 found thinner ozone at low O₂
background.detail: Earlier 3D simulations suggested lower ozone columns at low O₂ than classic 1D results.

background.headline: First 1D vs 3D comparison
background.detail: Ji et al. compared the Kasting model with WACCM6 and ROCKE-3D and found differences in ozone columns.

background.headline: 3D transport moves ozone poleward
background.detail: The Brewer–Dobson circulation carries ozone from the tropics, where it is made, toward the poles.

setup.headline: Four open-source 1D codes vs 3D WACCM6
setup.detail: Atmos, Photochem, VULCAN and the Kasting model, compared side by side with the WACCM6 chemistry-climate model under matched conditions. Earlier comparisons covered only the Kasting model.

setup.headline: 1D runs fed WACCM6's temperatures
setup.detail: Global-mean pressure-temperature profiles and boundary conditions from WACCM6 are used in every 1D model, so differences come from the models themselves.

setup.headline: O₂ from 0.1% to 150% of today
setup.detail: Eight oxygen levels, with zenith angles of 45–60° in the 1D runs (main results at 48.2°).

setup.headline: Errors traced to UV damage and spectra
setup.detail: TUV turns each ozone profile into surface DNA damage; PSG turns Proxima Centauri b atmospheres into transmission spectra.

setup.headline: Defaults kept on purpose
setup.detail: Each 1D code keeps its own default chemistry, solar spectrum and humidity scheme, as a typical user would. The differences therefore mix real physics with configuration choices.

setup.headline: WACCM6 is the reference, not the truth
setup.detail: WACCM6 is one of the best CMIP6 ozone models, but it lacks scattering in the Schumann–Runge bands and keeps modern surface conditions at every O₂ level.

method.headline: How do the ozone columns compare?
method.detail: total O₃ column vs O₂ level for each model, across 1D zenith angles of 45–60°.

results.headline: Models broadly agree
results.detail: All fall near the WACCM6 range; Kasting and Photochem are closest.

results.headline: 1D codes predict more ozone than WACCM6
results.detail: Below ~5% PAL, Photochem, Atmos and VULCAN sit above the WACCM6 range. Kasting stays closest and only diverges below 1% PAL. The gap grows as O₂ falls.

results.headline: Peak ozone density differs up to 6×
results.detail: Stratospheric peak densities differ by 1.18× at 100% PAL, rising to 1.85×, 2.8× and 6.0× at 10%, 1% and 0.1% PAL.

method.headline: Why do they differ? Making ozone
method.detail: compare O₂ photolysis (odd-oxygen production), O₃-forming rate coefficients and input solar spectra.

results.headline: Where O₂ is split matters more than how much
results.detail: Total photolysis agrees within 30–60%, but the shape and height of the peak differ by up to 2.1× at 1% PAL.

results.headline: Formation rate coefficients differ 1.2–1.3×
results.detail: Same temperatures, different rates for O + O₂ + M → O₃.

results.headline: Solar spectrum alone explains some, not all
results.detail: Swapping Photochem's solar spectrum for WACCM6's lowers its O₃ by 1.03× (100% PAL) to 1.5× (0.1% PAL), not enough to close the gap.

method.headline: Why do they differ? Destroying ozone
method.detail: compare HOₓ, NOₓ and water-vapour profiles that drive catalytic O₃ loss.

results.headline: HOₓ differs up to ~250×
results.detail: Lower-stratospheric HOₓ disagrees most at modern O₂, then converges toward 1% PAL.

results.headline: NOₓ close, but NO₂ too low in 1D
results.detail: Total NOₓ agrees within 3×, but 1D models underpredict NO₂ near and above the ozone peak.

results.headline: 1D can't get stratospheric water right
results.detail: Stratospheric H₂O is set by the cold tropical tropopause, which a global average misses. Photochem and VULCAN reach 14–16.5 ppmv vs WACCM6's 3.7.

method.headline: Does 3D circulation change the column?
method.detail: WACCM6 winds and overturning circulation, plus runs with a 12-hour day and zero tilt.

results.headline: Deep overturning weakens at low O₂
results.detail: The deep Brewer–Dobson branch fades by 0.1% PAL, so less ozone is carried out of the tropics.

results.headline: Changing rotation & tilt: −7% ozone
results.detail: 169 → 158 DU, with O₂ photolysis changing by under 3%.

results.headline: Changing rotation & tilt: −15% ozone
results.detail: 59.5 → 50.6 DU. Dynamics alone changes the column, which 1D models cannot capture.

method.headline: Do other inputs matter?
method.detail: sweeps of surface albedo, methane (0.1–10×) and the young Sun's spectrum (Appendix B).

results.headline: Albedo and methane: small effects
results.detail: Albedo changes the column by ~3%. Methane's effect is small, and its sign depends on the O₂ level.

results.headline: Young Sun: minor without climate feedback
results.detail: Photochemistry alone barely changes.

results.headline: Young Sun doubles ozone: 44 → 94 DU
results.detail: With climate coupled (Atmos), a fainter Sun cools and dries the air, reducing HOₓ destruction. The main runs are uncoupled, so they miss feedbacks like this.

method.headline: What does it mean for life on the surface?
method.detail: TUV surface DNA-damage dose for each model's atmosphere, relative to WACCM6's global mean, overhead Sun.

results.headline: 1D gives 1.8–8.1× less DNA damage
results.detail: Early Earth's surface may have been harsher than 1D models suggest.

results.headline: Using the equator narrows the gap
results.detail: Against WACCM6's equatorial column, damage rises again by 1.1–1.5×, most at 10% PAL.

method.headline: What does it mean for exoplanet spectra?
method.detail: tidally locked Proxima Centauri b with Atmos, Photochem, VULCAN and WACCM6; PSG transmission spectra, 0.2–12 µm.

results.headline: Ozone builds up as O₂ drops: 952 DU
results.detail: At 0.1% PAL, transport to the nightside, where O₃ isn't destroyed by sunlight, lets it accumulate.

results.headline: Ozone falls with O₂: 19–71 DU
results.detail: 1D codes can't represent the day–night contrast of a tidally locked planet.

results.headline: Same planet, different ozone features
results.detail: The 0.25, 0.6 and 9.65 µm O₃ features differ in strength between models. The 0.6 µm feature almost vanishes with VULCAN's sulphur network.

results.headline: One boundary condition: 245 → 8352 DU
results.detail: Dropping O₃ surface deposition in Photochem (unknown for exoplanets) inflates the column ~34×.

conclusion.headline: 1D codes overpredict ozone at low O₂
conclusion.detail: Relative to 3D WACCM6, at ≤10% PAL, growing as O₂ falls. 1D spread alone is 1.6× at 100% PAL and 2.5× at 0.1% PAL.

conclusion.headline: Many causes, no single fix
conclusion.detail: O₂ photolysis, chemical networks and rates, water vapour, and 3D transport all contribute.

conclusion.headline: Early-Earth UV may have been harsher
conclusion.detail: Studies that take surface UV from 1D models (S-MIF thresholds, banded iron formations, early life) may inherit the bias.

conclusion.headline: Ozone is a poor proxy for O₂
conclusion.detail: Model differences add degeneracy even when the host star's spectrum is known.

conclusion.headline: Caveat: not true Proterozoic conditions
conclusion.detail: Modern surface fluxes and continents are held fixed while O₂ changes, so these are idealised scenarios.

conclusion.headline: Next: update photolysis, compare 3D models
conclusion.detail: Adopt the latest Schumann–Runge treatment, report boundary conditions fully, and run 3D intercomparisons (e.g. CUISINES).

glossary.meaning: Present Atmospheric Level: O₂ as a fraction of today's 21%. 1% PAL ≈ 0.21% O₂.
Measure of ozone column thickness; today's Earth has roughly 300 DU.
Treats the atmosphere as one averaged vertical column. Fast and chemically detailed, but no winds, seasons or day–night.
Simulates the whole globe with winds, seasons, clouds and day–night; slow and expensive (here WACCM6).
Wavelengths (175–205 nm) where O₂ absorbs UV in a complex, temperature-dependent way; crucial for making ozone.
Angle of the Sun from overhead. 1D models pick one average value, which itself changes the ozone result.
Hydrogen and nitrogen radical families that destroy ozone in catalytic cycles.
Slow stratospheric overturning that carries ozone from the tropics toward the poles.
The cold tropical tropopause freezes out water, setting how wet the stratosphere is.

other_questions.short: What do the model differences mean for early-Earth habitability and exoplanet observations?
other_questions.detail: Surface UV on the early Earth and the O₃ signal in exoplanet spectra are usually computed with these same 1D codes.

answer.short: A lot: 1D codes give 1.5–8× less surface DNA damage than WACCM6 at low O₂, and change Proxima b's O₃ features.
answer.detail: Early-Earth UV may have been harsher than 1D studies assume, and O₃ becomes a less reliable proxy for O₂ because the choice of model adds its own uncertainty.

equations.meaning: How ozone is made (the Chapman mechanism): UV splits O₂, and each O atom joins an O₂ with a third molecule carrying off energy.
equations.symbols: hν = a photon, M = any third molecule (usually N₂ or O₂).

equations.meaning: Ozone is split by sunlight (and quickly re-formed); the direct O + O₃ reaction removes it for good, but slowly.
A catalytic cycle: the radical X is given back at the end, so one radical can destroy thousands of ozone molecules.
equations.symbols: X = a radical such as OH, H, NO or Cl.

equations.meaning: How water vapour feeds the HOₓ radicals that destroy ozone.
The biologically effective dose: the surface UV spectrum weighted by how much each wavelength damages DNA.
equations.symbols: E = spectral irradiance at the surface, W = biological weighting function.
